svg.aria-label: Chart: the four multi-region Kafka topologies placed on a single spectrum of how wide the duplicate window is when you fail over. At the left, a stretched cluster has no duplicate window at all, because there is only one offset address space and nothing to translate, but it is bounded by geography — it needs round-trip times under 50 to 100 milliseconds and a third site to hold the quorum, which confines it to a metro rather than a continent. In the middle, mirrored active-passive and mirrored active-active — the same replication mechanism, differing only in whether the second region also serves — both land in the same place, a window of seconds set by the offset-sync interval and biased backwards on purpose; they differ from each other on other axes, not on this one. At the right, producer dual-write has an unbounded and unmeasurable window, because two independent writes share no sequence to reconcile against. Below the spectrum, a second curve shows the latency charged to every acknowledged write, which runs the opposite way: high for the stretched cluster where each write waits for a cross-site round trip, near zero for the two mirrored options where replication sits off the write path, and high again for dual-write which pays the produce cost N times. The two curves cross in the middle, where the mirrored options sit. The closing caption reads: you are not choosing an availability tier, you are choosing how much reconciliation you will have to build.
